solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nevertheless, is not to be satisfied with just part

definitions.meaning: used as an adverb meaning in spite of everything, all the same

definitions.text: is not to be satisfied with just part
definitions.meaning: read literally, someone who is seeking the whole lot and wants every bit of it

explanation.surface: A grudging remark about someone who will never settle for a share of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as the idiom for 'all the same' and, taken word by word, as chasing the whole.

clue.text: Remained perfectly still and went cold all over?

definitions.meaning: to stop dead and not move a muscle
turned to ice, became chilled through

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both stopping motionless in fright and becoming solid with cold.

clue.text: Tries to correct extreme spin

indicators.note: correcting something puts it right by rearranging it, so the letters of extreme and spin are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to fix a wildly excessive bit of political spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like a verb but is the noun: trials or tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Trials or tests carried out to see what happens are attempts, in noun form.

clue.text: CIA try to resolve crime

indicators.note: to resolve can mean to break down into parts and reform, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: American intelligence attempts to solve a criminal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is part of the fodder, not a link word: CIA TRY TO gives the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is a wicked, shocking act, an extreme kind of offence.

clue.text: Rocky island with nowhere to relax

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaky, telling us to shake up the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A barren rocky island offers nowhere at all to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' belongs to the fodder: ISLAND plus NOWHERE TO gives fifteen letters; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop being formal and enjoy oneself freely, i.e. unwind.

clue.text: Spare part of a loaf for dinner

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they can give up a bit of bread for the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare money or time is to be able to give it without hardship, as in 'can you spare it'.

clue.text: For each expert, a pastry dish in brought in

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: an ace is a highly skilled expert
a pie is a dish baked in pastry

explanation.surface: Each specialist is served a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a stray 'in' before 'brought in'; it is read as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Used after a number or price, it means for every one, individually.

clue.text: Cool an ardent admirer

definitions.meaning: to cool something by moving air over it
an enthusiast or devotee of a star or team

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means wafting air to cool, as a noun a devoted follower.

clue.text: Vocal registers

parts.note: suggests singing ranges, but means registers of names that are called out loud to take attendance

explanation.walkthrough: 'registers' looks like a range of the singing voice; here it is a list of names, checked by speaking each one.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance checks in which each name on a list is read out are spoken registers.

clue.text: A good conductor controls the beat

definitions.meaning: a metal that carries electricity well, not an orchestra leader
a police officer patrols and keeps order on a beat

explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' and 'beat' suggest music; one sense is a metal, the other a policeman, informal British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal conducts electricity well, and the slang word names a police officer patrolling a round.

clue.text: The eternal musical instrument?

parts.note: the 'eternal' version is the love affair of three people; the same word names a percussion instrument

explanation.walkthrough: The 'eternal' kind is the classic love tangle of three people; the same word names a metal percussion instrument struck with a beater.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided steel percussion piece shares its name with the phrase for a three-way romance.

clue.text: Display stand

definitions.meaning: to show or carry visibly, as a coin shows an image
to tolerate or put up with

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to carry a visible mark and also to endure or put up with something.

clue.text: Study to gain knowledge and moral insight

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
science originally meant knowledge in general, from Latin scientia

explanation.surface: Learning brings both information and a sense of right and wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner sense of right and wrong is a moral faculty of understanding.

clue.text: Having no saving graces?

parts.note: a 'saving grace' is a redeeming quality, but here it means someone with no inclination to save money

explanation.walkthrough: A saving grace is normally a redeeming feature; read literally it is thrift, and a person lacking it spends wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendthrift who wastes money lacks any habit of thrift.

clue.text: Senior churchmen easily shocked by a setback

parts.note: a prim person is prudish and easily offended
read as two parts, the word set followed by back, telling us to reverse the word set

explanation.surface: Prudish bishops are scandalised by a reversal of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' looks like a misfortune but is read as an instruction: the word SET, turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: Archbishops who are the leading clergy of a country are given this title.

clue.text: Discount accepted for a bad egg

indicators.note: the discount takes in or accepts the other word inside it

parts.note: a rebate is a reduction or partial refund
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: A cheat gets a price reduction approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms describe an unprincipled, disreputable person.

clue.text: List of lists

definitions.meaning: to lean over to one side, as a ship does
the lists were the arena for jousting, so a joust in them is a charge with a lance

explanation.walkthrough: The lists were the fenced ground for medieval jousting; the word also means a lean.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a lean to one side and also a jousting charge, the business of the lists.

clue.text: Rash outbreak?

parts.note: looks like a spotty skin eruption, but means a widespread outbreak of disease

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint but works as 'sudden and widespread'.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease spreading quickly through a community is a sudden widespread outbreak.

clue.text: Short run which distinguishes slow bowlers

definitions.meaning: a quick drive or ride for pleasure
in cricket slow bowlers turn the ball off the pitch

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slower bowlers rely on turning the ball rather than pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief outing in a car, and the turn on the ball that marks slow bowling.

clue.text: Pop back to extol value

indicators.note: back means the word for father is read the other way round

parts.note: pop and pa are both informal words for father
to extol is to praise highly

explanation.surface: Dad comes home to sing someone's merits.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess the worth of something is to estimate its value.

clue.text: Having gone off thoroughly confused

definitions.meaning: rotten, as an egg goes bad

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a rotten egg and also a muddled brain.

clue.text: Thought one had respected other people's feelings

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, carefully reasoned, as in a careful opinion

definitions.text: one had respected other people's feelings
definitions.meaning: having taken others into account, been thoughtful of them

explanation.definitionFit: It means carefully thought out, and is also the past tense of taking others into account.

clue.text: Trees spring back around south

indicators.note: the reversed spring goes around the letter for south
back says the word for spring is read the other way round

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Trees bounce back into place around the southern side.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an old poetic word for aspens, not the snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic name for the aspen, a poplar tree, gives this plural.

clue.text: Swan to circle about and tidy her feathers

indicators.note: the swan's word circles or surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A swan paddles in a circle and then grooms herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds groom and smooth their plumage with the beak; 'her' fits the female swan.

clue.text: Crushing defeat later, perhaps, in court

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of later may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A heavy loss is suffered later, possibly in a lawcourt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a lawcourt but is the verb of romance; 'perhaps' signals the reshuffle of ATERL.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's final battle gave its name to any decisive, final rout.

clue.text: A priest that's about, about fifty?

indicators.note: the second about means around, enclosing the Roman numeral
about here means turned round, so the letters for that is are reversed

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A clergyman about whom we ask: is he roughly fifty?
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'about' reverses IE to EI; the second puts it around L.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible he was the priest at Shiloh who brought up Samuel.

clue.text: Having all-round defence in depth?

parts.note: military 'defence in depth' is layered, but here it is a deep water-filled ditch encircling a castle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence in depth' is a military idiom; here it is literally a deep ditch of water around a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle surrounded by a water-filled ditch is protected on every side by a deep barrier.

clue.text: A time in which love and pride are mingled

indicators.note: letters that are mingled are mixed together into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An era when affection and self-esteem blend together.
explanation.definitionFit: An era or span of time in history is a stretch of time.

clue.text: Arrest adolescent providing narcotic substance, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are said out loud and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to arrest, and a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: Police detain a youngster for supplying drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The addictive alkaloid in tobacco is a drug, a substance with narcotic effects.
